classification.difficultyReason: Derive the trapezium height using Pythagoras, then combine cross-sectional area and rectangular faces to calculate surface area and volume.

content.prompt:
The cross-section $ABCD$ of the prism shown is an isosceles trapezium with $AB=8\text{ cm}$, $DC=14\text{ cm}$, $AD=BC=5\text{ cm}$ and $AE=20\text{ cm}$.

Calculate:

spec.sourceRegion: Question 4, trapezoidal prism at the right
spec.description: Unshaded trapezoidal prism with front vertices A, B, C, D and rear upper-left vertex E. Three dashed hidden edges meet at the rear lower-left vertex. Ordinary source blue and red edge strokes become black; dashes retain the hidden-edge distinction. Projection coordinates express the source view and are not numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: Front cross-section is an isosceles trapezium with parallel AB and DC; corresponding front and rear vertices are joined along the prism. AB=8 cm, DC=14 cm, AD=BC=5 cm and AE=20 cm are supplied in the stem only.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied geometry and labels remain visible; no calculated height, area or volume is shown.

answer.worked:
The equal overhangs of the longer parallel side are each $\frac{(14-8)}{2}=3\text{ cm}$. Let the perpendicular height of the trapezium be $h$.

$$\begin{align*}h^2&=5^2-3^2\\h^2&=16\\h&=4\text{ cm}\\A_{ABCD}&=\frac12(8+14)\times4\\A_{ABCD}&=44\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: the surface area of the prism

answer.worked:
The surface consists of two trapezia and four rectangles.

$$\begin{align*}S&=2\times44+(8+14+5+5)\times20\\S&=88+32\times20\\S&=88+640\\S&=728\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
